If both Assertion and Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false

19.sol: The main function of sieve tube is the transport of food products from green and storage organs of the plant to other organs of the plant. The sieve elements are sieve tubes arranged one above the other and have sieve plates (obligue or transverse perforated septa) on their end walls. The cytoplasm occur in the form of a thin living layer along the inner side of cellulose wall. The nucleus disappears in mature sieve elements.

24.subject: Botany
24.text: Select the correct pair amongst the following
options: Spring wood – light colour, high density
Spring wood – dark colour, low density
Autumn wood – light colour, high density
Autumn wood – dark colour, high density
24.sol: The yearly growth of secondary xylem is distinct in the area which experiences two seasons, one favourable (spring or rainy season) and the other unfavourable (autumn, winter and dry summer). The wood formed in a single year consists of two types of wood, spring wood and autumn wood. The spring or early wood is much wider than the autumn or late wood. It is lighter in colour and of lower density. Spring wood consists of larger and wider xylem elements. The autumn or late wood is dark coloured and of higher density. It contains compactly arranged smaller and narrower elements which have comparatively thicker walls. In autumn wood, tracheids and fibres are more abundant than those found in the spring wood.

172.text: Three of the following statements regarding cell organelles are correct while one is wrong. Which one is wrong?
options: Lysosomes are double membraned vesicles budded off from Golgi apparatus and contain digestive enzymes.
Endoplasmic reticulum consists of a network of membranous tubules and helps in transport, synthesis and secretion.
Leucoplasts are bound by two membranes, lack pigment but contain their own DNA and protein synthesizing machinery.
Sphaerosomes are single membrane bound and are associated with synthesis and storage of lipids.
172.sol: Lysosomes are roughly spherical bodies bounded by a single membrane. They are manufactured by the Golgi apparatus. Lysosomes are small membrane bound vesicles in the cytoplasm of cells which contain toxic enzymes. When a cell dies, these membranes rupture and the enzymes are released. They break down the cells structure, and the debris is removed.

Given: Distance between two charges $=d$ and dielectric constant $(k)=2$. Force between two charged spheres $(F)=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \times \frac{q_1 q_2}{r_2}$, where $\varepsilon_0$ is permitivity of free space. Force for a medium with dielectric constant $k$,

Assertion : Smaller the organism higher is the rate of metabolism per gram weight.
Reason : The heart rate of a six month old baby is much lower than that of an old person.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1946.sol: The basal metabolic rate (BMR) is defined as the energy requirement of the human body at rest and reflects the caloric needs of the body. BMR can be determined by total body weight and the amount of muscle mass. BMR is inversely related with the weight or volume of an organism, i.e. smaller the organism, higher is the basal metabolic rate and vice versa. Heart rate of six month old baby is \(110-112\) beats \(/ \mathrm{min}\). Though it is higher than normal adult person, but it is lower than the old person. At the age of 60 , a man may have maximum heart rate of 160 beats \(/ \mathrm{min}\) (avg 120 beats \(/ \mathrm{min}\) ).

amino acids are catabolised in kidney to form glucose
amino acids are discharged in blood stream from liver

4428.text:
$50mL$ of $0. 02MNaOH$ solution is mixed with $50mL$ of $0. 06M$ acetic acid solution, the $pH$ of the resulting solution is_________
$( pKa$ of acetic acid is $4. 76, log5 = 0. 70 )$.&
4428.sol:
When a strong base is added to a weak acid solution, it results in the formation of a salt. Here, acid is present in a limiting reagent and base is present in excess amounts. So, by using the pH formula:

$\begin{cases}pH & = & pKa + log\left[salt\right]\left[acid\right] \\ pH & = & 4 . 46 + log\left[0 . 02 \times 50\right]\left[( 0 . 06 - 0 . 02 ) \times 50\right] \\ pH & = & 4 . 76 + log ( 0 . 5 ) \\ pH & = & 4 . 46\end{cases}$

${S}_{2}{O3}^{2 -} + {CN}^{-}\overset{HCl}{→}{SCN}^{-} + {SO3}^{-}$

${FeCl}_{3} + {SCN}^{-} \to Fe{( SCN )}^{2 +} ( bloodredcolour )$

Hence, the solution is cooled and acidified with $HCl$ and this solution with iron $( III )$ chloride produces blood-red colour solution.

5486.text: A gaseous mixture of 3 gases \(A, B\) and \(C\) has a pressure \(10 \mathrm{~atm}\). The total number of moles are 10. If partial pressure of gases \(A\) and \(B\) are \(3 \mathrm{~atm}\) and \(1 \mathrm{~atm}\) respectively and if molar mass of gas \(C\) is 2 . Calculate the weight of \(C\) in the mixture.
5486.sol:
(i) \(p=p_A+p_B+p_C\) (Dalton's law)
\((\because p=\text{ total pressure, } p^{\prime}=\text{ partial }\)
pressure,
\(\begin{aligned}
& n=\text{ number of moles }) \\
\Rightarrow & p_C=p-\left(p_A+p_B\right)=10-(3+1)=6 \mathrm{~atm}
\end{aligned}\)
(ii)
\(\begin{aligned}
& p_C=\frac{n_C}{n_A+n_B+n_C} \times p \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{n_C}{10} \times 10=n_C \\
& \Rightarrow \quad n_C=p_C=6
\end{aligned}\)
(iii) Weight of \(C\) in the mixture \(=n_C \times\) molar mass of \(C\) \(=6 \times 2=12 \mathrm{~g}\)

11410.text: If the sum of the roots of the quadratic equations is 1 and sum of the squares of the roots is 13 , then find that equation.
11410.sol:
Let the roots of the quadratic equation are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) then it is given that
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\beta& =1 \text{ and } \alpha^2+\beta^2=13 \\
\therefore \quad \alpha \beta& =\frac{1}{2}\left[(\alpha+\beta)^2-\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2\right)\right]=\frac{1}{2}[1-13]=-6
\end{aligned}$$\)
So, equation of required quadratic is
\(x²-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha \beta=0 \Rightarrow x²-x-6=0.\)

According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes, the masses of the substances deposited are proportional to their equivalent weights.

$\dfrac{W_{Ca}}{W_{Mg}} = \dfrac{E_{Ca}}{E_{Mg}}$

Equivalent weight of Mg, $E_{Mg} = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12$

Equivalent weight of Ca, $E_{Ca} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20$

Given $W_{Mg} = 4.8$ g.

$\dfrac{W_{Ca}}{4.8} = \dfrac{20}{12}$

$W_{Ca} = \dfrac{20}{12} \times 4.8 = 8.0$ g

Answer: $8.0$ g

For the reaction,
$2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}+b \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-}+c \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow x \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}+y \mathrm{CO}_2+z \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ Find $b, c, x, y$ and $z$
20541.sol:
The given redox reaction is $2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} + b \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} + c \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow x \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + y \mathrm{CO}_2 + z \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

The oxidation half-reaction is $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}_2 + 2e^{-}$.

The reduction half-reaction is $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} + 8 \mathrm{H}^{+} + 5e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 4 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

To balance the electrons, multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 5 and the reduction half-reaction by 2:

$5 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 10 \mathrm{CO}_2 + 10e^{-}$

$2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} + 16 \mathrm{H}^{+} + 10e^{-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

Adding the two half-reactions gives:

$2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-} + 5 \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4^{2-} + 16 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{CO}_2 + 8 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$

Comparing this with the given equation, we find $b=5$, $c=16$, $x=2$, $y=10$, and $z=8$.

Answer: $b=5, \quad c=16, \quad x=2, \quad y=10, \quad z=8$

20924.subject: Mathematics
20924.text: The curve $4 y=3 x^4-2 x^2$ attains -------- at the points $x=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $x=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
options: a minimum value and a maximum value respectively
a maximum value and a minimum value respectively
20924.sol:
Given the curve $4y = 3x^4 - 2x^2$, we have $y = \dfrac{3}{4}x^4 - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2$.

To find the critical points, we calculate the first derivative with respect to $x$:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{4}(4x^3) - \dfrac{1}{2}(2x) = 3x^3 - x = x(3x^2 - 1)$.

Setting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, we get $x = 0$, $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, and $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

To determine the nature of these points, we calculate the second derivative:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9x^2 - 1$.

Evaluating at $x = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:
$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) - 1 = 3 - 1 = 2$.

Since $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} > 0$ at both $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, the function attains a local minimum value at both points.

Answer: both minimum values

21005.subject: Mathematics
21005.text: Area of the region bounded by the curve $y=\cos x$ between $x=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\pi$ is-----
21005.sol:
The area $A$ bounded by the curve $y = \cos x$ between $x = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x = \pi$ is given by the integral $A = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi} |\cos x| dx$.

The function $\cos x$ is positive in the interval $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$ and negative in the interval $[\pi/2, \pi]$.

Therefore, the integral is split as $A = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \cos x dx + \int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} -\cos x dx$.

Evaluating the first integral: $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \cos x dx = [\sin x]_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} = \sin(\pi/2) - \sin(-\pi/2) = 1 - (-1) = 2$.

Evaluating the second integral: $-\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} \cos x dx = -[\sin x]_{\pi/2}^{\pi} = -(\sin \pi - \sin(\pi/2)) = -(0 - 1) = 1$.

The total area is $A = 2 + 1 = 3$ sq units.

Answer: 3 sq units

21069.subject: Mathematics
21069.text: The remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$ is
21069.sol:
We need to find the remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$.

We can write $7^{103}$ as $7 \cdot 7^{102} = 7 \cdot (7^2)^{51}$.

We know that $7^2 = 49 \equiv -1 \pmod{25}$.

Raising both sides to the power of $51$, we get:

$(7^2)^{51} \equiv (-1)^{51} \pmod{25}$

$7^{102} \equiv -1 \pmod{25}$

Multiplying both sides by $7$, we get:

$7^{103} \equiv -7 \pmod{25}$

To find the positive remainder, we add $25$ to $-7$:

$-7 + 25 = 18$

Thus, the remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$ is $18$.

Answer: $18$

21944.text: Three of the six vertices of a regular hexagon are chosen at random. The probability that the triangle with three vertices is equilateral equals
21944.sol:
The total number of ways to choose 3 vertices out of 6 is given by ^{6}C_{3}$.

^{6}C_{3} = \dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 20$.

A regular hexagon has vertices labeled $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ in order. A triangle formed by these vertices is equilateral if the indices of the vertices are in arithmetic progression with a common difference of 2. The possible sets of vertices are $\{1, 3, 5\}$ and $\{2, 4, 6\}$.

There are exactly 2 such triangles.

The probability is the ratio of the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes:

$P = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{10}$

25098.text: According to kinetic theory of gases
options:
collisions are always elastic

heavier molecules transfer more momentum to the wall of the container

only a small number of molecules have very high velocity

between collisions, the molecules move in straight lines with constant velocities
25098.sol:

(b) If a gas molecule of man ' $m$ ' moving with speed ' $u$ ' collide to the wall of container, the change in momentum is $\Delta p=-2 \mathrm{mu}$. Therefore, heavier molecule will transfer more momentum to the wall as there will be greater change in momentum of the colliding gas malecule. However this was not postulated in kinetic theory of Gases.
(c) According to Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of molecular speed, very few molecules have either very high or very low speeds. Most of the molecules moves in a specific, intermediate speed range.
(d) According to kinetic theory of gases, a gas molecule moves in straight line unless it collide with another molecular or to the wall of container and change in momentum is observed only after collision.

27018.subject: Chemistry
27018.text:
An organic compound "$x$" where molar ratio of C, O and H are equal, on treatment with $50\%$ KOH under reflux followed by acidification produced "$y$". The most likely structure of "$y$" is:
[Molar mass of '$x$' is $58$ g mol$^{-1}$]
options: $O = C - OH, \, CH_2 - OH$ (with C-C bond)
27018.sol:
Given the molar ratio of C, O, and H in compound $x$ is equal, the empirical formula is $CHO$.

Empirical mass $= 12 + 1 + 16 = 29$ g mol$^{-1}$.

Since the molar mass of $x$ is $58$ g mol$^{-1}$, the molecular formula is $(CHO)_2$ or $C_2H_2O_2$.

The structure of $x$ is glyoxal, $OHC-CHO$.

Treatment of glyoxal with $50\%$ KOH under reflux results in an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction. One aldehyde group is oxidized to a carboxylate ion, and the other is reduced to a primary alcohol.

$OHC-CHO \xrightarrow{50\% \text{ KOH}} HOCH_2-COO^{-}K^{+}$

Subsequent acidification yields glycolic acid ($y$).

$HOCH_2-COO^{-}K^{+} \xrightarrow{H^{+}} HOCH_2-COOH$

The structure of $y$ is $HO-CH_2-COOH$.

Answer: $O = C - OH, \, CH_2 - OH$ (with C-C bond)

29813.text:
The descending order of acidity for the following carboxylic acid is-
(A) ${CH}_{3}COOH$
(B) ${F}_{3}C - COOH$
(C) ${ClCH}_{2} - COOH$
(D) ${FCH}_{2} - COOH$
(E) ${BrCH}_{2} - COOH$

29813.sol:
The correct order of acidic strength of the given carboxylic acids will be decided by the stability of their conjugate bases. The $+ I$ effect of ${CH}_{3}$ group destabilises the carboxylate anion. But the $- I$ effect of halogen substituted methyl group stabilises the carboxylate anion. Higher the $- I$ effect of the halogen substituted methyl group, higher the acidic strength of the corresponding acid.
$∴$ Correct order of acidic strength is
${F}_{3}C - \mathop{COOH}_{\text{(B)}} > {FCH}_{2} - \mathop{COOH}_{\text{(D)}} > \mathop{{CICH}_{2} - COOH}_{\left(C\right)} > \mathop{{BrCH}_{2} - COOH}_{\left(E\right)} > \mathop{{CH}_{3} - COOH}_{\left(A\right)}$

30215.subject: Chemistry
30215.text: The correct order of the rate of the reaction for the following reaction with respect to nucleophiles is : $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{Br}+\mathrm{Nu}^{\ominus} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{Nu}+\mathrm{Br}^{\ominus}$
30215.sol:
For the SN2 reaction CH₃Br + Nu⁻, nucleophilicity in aprotic solvents is determined by basicity and polarizability.
⁻OH (hydroxide) is the strongest nucleophile and base, making it highly reactive.
PhO⁻ (phenoxide) is a good nucleophile with reasonable basicity.
CH₃COO⁻ (acetate) is weakened by resonance stabilization of its negative charge across the C-O bonds, reducing its nucleophilicity.
ClO₄⁻ (perchlorate) is a very weak nucleophile, being the conjugate base of a strong acid (HClO₄).
The correct order of nucleophilicity is: ⁻OH > PhO⁻ > CH₃COO⁻ > ClO₄⁻, which matches option (3).

33674.text: The common tangent to the circles ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 4$ and ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 6x + 8y - 24 = 0$ also passes through the point:
33674.sol:
The centre and radius of the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ are respectively $\left(- g, - f\right)$ and $\sqrt{{g}^{2} + {f}^{2} - c} .

Let, for the circle${S}_{1}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 4$ centre ${C}_{1}: $\left(0, 0\right)$, {r}_{1} = 2$ units.

And, for the circle ${S}_{2}: {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 6x + 8y - 24 = 0$ centre

${C}_{2}$\left(- 3, - 4\right)$, {r}_{2} = \sqrt{{3}^{2} + {4}^{2} + 24} = 7units.

The distance between the $points \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right) and \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right) is$\sqrt{{$\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)$}^{2} + {$\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)$}^{2}}$

Hence, the distance between the centres of the circles is ${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = \sqrt{{$\left(- 3 - 0\right)$}^{2} + {$\left(- 4 - 0\right)$}^{2}} = 5$ units.

Also, \left|{r}_{1} - {r}_{2}\right| = 5$ units.

Since, ${C}_{1}{C}_{2} = \left|{r}_{1} - {r}_{2}\right|,$ hence both the circles touches each other internally.

Therefore, the common tangent is same as the radical axis of the two circles i.e. ${S}_{1} - {S}_{2} = 0$

Thus, the common tangent is ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 4 - \left({x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 6x + 8y - 24\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 6x - 8y + 20 = 0$

⇒ 3x + 4y - 10 = 0 .

Clearly, the $point \left(6, - 2\right) lies on the common tangent.

$

36282.subject: Mathematics
36282.text: If one end of a focal chord of the parabola, ${y}^{2} = 16x$ is at $\left(1, 4\right)$, then the length of this focal chord is
36282.sol:
The given parabola ${y}^{2} = 16x$ is of the form ${y}^{2} = 4ax,$ hence $a = 4$ and the focus of the parabola is $\left(a, 0\right) = \left(4, 0\right) .$

The equation of a line joining the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$ and $\left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$ is $y - {y}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{{y}_{2} - {y}_{1}}{{x}_{2} - {x}_{1}}\right)\left(x - {x}_{1}\right) .$

Therefore, equation of chord joining $P\left(1, 4\right)$ to focus $S\left(4, 0\right)$ is

$y - 0 = - \dfrac{4}{3}\left(x - 4\right)$

$⇒ 3y = - 4x + 16$

$⇒ 4x + 3y - 16 = 0$

To find the points where this line will cut the parabola put $x = \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{16}$ from the parabola into the line, to get

$4\left(\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{16}\right) + 3y - 16 = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} + 12y - 64 = 0$

$⇒ \left(y + 16\right)\left(y - 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ y = - 16$ or $y = 4$

And $x = \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{16}$

$⇒ x = 16$ or $x = 1$

Thus, the points are $\left(1, 4\right)$ and $\left(16, - 16\right),$ but $\left(1, 4\right)$ is the given point $P .$

$⇒ Q = \left(16, - 16\right)$

The distance between the points $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right) \text{ and } \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)}^{2}}$

So, the length of focal chord $PQ$ is

$PQ = \sqrt{{\left(16 - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(- 16 - 4\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{225 + 400} = \sqrt{625} = 25$ units.

42420.subject: Physics
42420.text: A ball of mass $m$ is thrown vertically upward. Another ball of mass $2m$ is thrown an angle $\theta$ with the vertical. Both the balls stay in air for the same period of time. The ratio of the heights attained by the two balls respectively is $\dfrac{1}{x}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
42420.sol:
When the first ball of mass $m$ is projected vertically upwards, the second ball of mass $2m$ makes an angle $\theta$ with the vertical.

The time of flight is the same for both the balls.

Then, ${T}_{1} = {T}_{2}$ $⇒ \dfrac{2{u}_{1}}{g} = \dfrac{2{u}_{2}sin\theta}{g}$

$⇒ {u}_{1} = {u}_{2}sin\theta . . . \left(1\right)$

Maximum height of projectile is given by $H = \dfrac{{u}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$

Ratio of the heights is $\dfrac{{H}_{1}}{{H}_{2}} = {u}_{1}^{2}{u}_{2}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$, we have

$⇒ \dfrac{{H}_{1}}{{H}_{2}} = 1$.

Thus, $x = 1$.

44430.text: A wire of length $30cm$, stretched between rigid supports, has it's ${n}^{th}$ and ${\left(n + 1\right)}^{th}$ harmonics at $400Hz$ and $450Hz$, respectively. If tension in the string is $2700N$, it's linear mass density is _____ $kg{m}^{- 1}$.
44430.sol:
Frequency of ${n}^{th}$ harmonic is $\dfrac{nv}{2l} = 400 ⇒ \dfrac{nv}{0 . 6} = 400 . . . \left(1\right)$

And frequency of ${\left(n + 1\right)}^{th}$ harmonic is $\dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)v}{2l} = 450 ⇒ \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)v}{0 . 6} = 450 . . . \left(2\right)$, here, $v$ is speed of wave on string.

From equation $\left(1\right)$, we have

$n = \dfrac{400 \times 0 . 6}{v}$

Putting in equation $\left(2\right)$,

$⇒ \left[\dfrac{0 . 6 \times 400}{v} + 1\right]\dfrac{v}{0 . 6} = 450$

$⇒ \left[400 + \dfrac{v}{0 . 6}\right] = 450$

$⇒ v = 30m{s}^{- 1}$

Speed of wave on string is stated as $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}} = 30$, here, $\mu$ is linear mass density.

So, $\mu = \dfrac{T}{{v}^{2}} = \dfrac{2700}{900} ⇒ \mu = 3kg{m}^{- 1}$

47292.subject: Biology
47292.text:
Read the following statements about Funaria and select the options which are correct.
a) Gametophyte is the dominant plant body.
b) The sporophyte is differentiated into foot, seta and capsule.
c) The gemmae are asexual, green, multicellular buds found on the thallus.
d) The sporophyte has independent existence.
47292.sol:
Funaria belongs to the class Bryopsida (mosses) of bryophytes.

Statement a is correct because in all bryophytes, including Funaria, the main plant body is the gametophyte, which is haploid and dominant.

Statement b is correct because the sporophyte of Funaria is well-differentiated into a foot, seta, and capsule.

Statement c is incorrect because gemmae are asexual reproductive structures found in liverworts (like Marchantia), not in mosses like Funaria.

Statement d is incorrect because the sporophyte in bryophytes is not free-living; it remains attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.

Thus, statements a and b are correct.

Answer: a and b

Focal length of lens \( =+18.75 $\mathrm{~cm}$\)

2 _ Lone pair and 2 _ Bond pair of electrons
2 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons
1 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons
55763.sol:
The central atom in $\text{BrF}_3$ is Bromine ($\text{Br}$).

Number of valence electrons in $\text{Br} = 7$.

Bromine forms $3$ single bonds with $3$ Fluorine atoms. Therefore, the number of bond pairs is $3$.

Number of electrons used in bonding $= 3$.

Remaining valence electrons on the central atom $= 7 - 3 = 4$.

Number of lone pairs $= \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$.

Thus, the central atom has $2$ lone pairs and $3$ bond pairs of electrons.

Answer: 2 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons

55771.subject: Chemistry
55771.text: Identify the type of hybridization of carbon that is attached to the OH group, in benzylic alcohol?
55771.sol:
The structure of benzylic alcohol is $C_6H_5-CH_2-OH$.

The carbon atom attached to the $-OH$ group is bonded to one carbon atom of the benzene ring, two hydrogen atoms, and one oxygen atom.

Since it forms exactly four sigma bonds and has zero lone pairs, its steric number is $4$.

Therefore, the hybridization of this carbon atom is $sp^3$.

Answer: $sp^3$

56024.subject: Chemistry
56024.text: The slope of a graph $\log [A]_t$ versus ' $t$ ' for first order reaction is $-2.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ s}^{-1}$. Find rate constant of the reaction?
56024.sol:
The integrated rate law for a first-order reaction is expressed as $\ln[A]_t = -kt + \ln[A]_0$.

Converting to base-10 logarithms using the identity $\ln x = 2.303 \log x$ yields:

$\log[A]_t = -\frac{k}{2.303}t + \log[A]_0$

This represents a linear relationship where the slope is $-\frac{k}{2.303}$.

Given the measured slope of the plot of $\log[A]_t$ versus time is $-2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrms^{-1}$, we equate:

$-\frac{k}{2.303} = -2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrms^{-1}$

Solving for the rate constant $k$:

$k = 2.303 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrms^{-1} = 5.7575 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrms^{-1}$

Rounded to three significant figures, $k \approx 5.76 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrms^{-1}$, confirming that option C is correct.

56449.subject: Chemistry
56449.sol:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) for cobalt in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is calculated using the standard formula:

$\text{EAN} = Z - \text{Oxidation State} + 2 \times (\text{Number of Ligands} \times \text{Denticity})$

Cobalt has atomic number $Z = 27$. In this complex, with six neutral $\mathrm{NH}_3$ ligands and an overall +3 charge, cobalt's oxidation state is +3.

Each $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is monodentate, donating one electron pair, contributing $6 \times 2 = 12$ electrons.
Substituting values: $\text{EAN} = 27 - 3 + 12 = 36$.

The Effective Atomic Number is $\boxed{36}$.

57582.subject: Chemistry
57582.text: Which of the following favors $\text{SN}^1$ reaction?
options: Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom
Small alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom
57582.sol:
The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate in its rate-determining step.

Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to the halogen atom (such as in tertiary alkyl halides) stabilize the resulting carbocation through the $+I$ inductive effect and hyperconjugation. Additionally, the steric crowding in the initial tetrahedral substrate is relieved when it forms a planar carbocation, which provides a driving force for the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism.

In contrast, a strong nucleophile and small alkyl groups favor the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism, while non-polar solvents do not favor the ionization step required for $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$.

Answer: Bulky alkyl groups on the carbon atom attached to halogen atom

The reaction proceeds via the formation of a brown chromium complex, which upon decomposition with water yields the corresponding aldehyde.

58036.subject: Chemistry
58036.text: Solubility of $\mathrm{Ca}_3\left(\mathrm{PO}_4\right)_2$ is 'S' mol $\mathrm{dm}^{-3}$. Find solubility product.
58036.sol:
The dissociation equilibrium for $\mathrm{Ca}_3\left(\mathrm{PO}_4\right)_2$ is:

$\mathrm{Ca}_3\left(\mathrm{PO}_4\right)_2 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3\mathrm{Ca}^{2+} (aq) + 2\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-} (aq)$

Let $S$ represent the molar solubility. The equilibrium concentrations become $[\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}] = 3S$ and $[\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}] = 2S$.

The solubility product expression is $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}]^3 [\mathrm{PO}_4^{3-}]^2$. Substituting the concentrations yields:

$K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (2S)^2 = 27S^3 \cdot 4S^2 = 108S^5$

The solubility product is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

59155.subject: Chemistry
59155.text: Which from following mixtures exhibits positive deviation from Raoult's law?
59155.sol:
Positive deviation from Raoult's law occurs when vapor pressure exceeds predictions due to weaker intermolecular attractions between mixture components than within pure substances.

Ethanol and acetone demonstrate this behavior: ethanol's strong hydrogen bonds are disrupted upon mixing, while acetone provides only dipole-dipole interactions. The resultant ethanol-acetone interactions are weaker than pure ethanol's hydrogen bonding, increasing vapor pressure.

Benzene-toluene mixtures exhibit near-ideal behavior with similar dispersion forces. Chloroform-acetone forms stronger hydrogen bonds ($\text{C-H}\cdots\text{O=C}$) than pure components, showing negative deviation. Phenol-aniline also demonstrates negative deviation through enhanced hydrogen bonding between phenolic hydrogens and aniline nitrogens.

Thus, only ethanol-acetone shows positive deviation.

60842.subject: Mathematics
60842.text: If $\mathrm{z}=x+$ iy is a complex number, then the equation $\left|\frac{\mathrm{z}+i}{\mathrm{z}-i}\right|=\sqrt{3}$ represents the
60842.sol:
Given the equation $\left|\frac{z+i}{z-i}\right|=\sqrt{3}$, substitute $z=x+iy$ to obtain:

$\left|\frac{x+i(y+1)}{x+i(y-1)}\right|=\sqrt{3}$.

Applying the modulus property $\left|\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right|=\frac{|z_1|}{|z_2|}$ and squaring both sides yields:

$\frac{x^2+(y+1)^2}{x^2+(y-1)^2}=3$.

Multiplying through by the denominator and expanding gives:

$x^2+y^2+2y+1=3x^2+3y^2-6y+3$.

Rearranging terms and simplifying leads to:

$2x^2+2y^2-8y+2=0$,

which reduces to $x^2+y^2-4y+1=0$ after division by 2.

Completing the square for $y$ results in:

$x^2+(y-2)^2=3$.

This represents a circle centered at $(0,2)$ with radius $\sqrt{3}$, corresponding to option B.

60845.subject: Mathematics
60845.sol:
To evaluate the expression $\frac{(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)^4}{(\sin\theta+i\cos\theta)^5}$, we apply De Moivre's Theorem and properties of complex numbers in polar form.

Using De Moivre's Theorem, the numerator simplifies to $\cos(4\theta) + i\sin(4\theta)$.
For the denominator, we first express $\sin\theta + i\cos\theta$ in polar form as $\cos(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta) + i\sin(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta)$.
Applying De Moivre's Theorem gives $(\sin\theta+i\cos\theta)^5 = \cos(\frac{5\pi}{2}-5\theta) + i\sin(\frac{5\pi}{2}-5\theta)$.

Dividing these complex numbers yields $\cos(9\theta-\frac{5\pi}{2}) + i\sin(9\theta-\frac{5\pi}{2})$.
Using the periodicity of trigonometric functions, this simplifies to $\cos(9\theta-\frac{\pi}{2}) + i\sin(9\theta-\frac{\pi}{2})$.

Applying the identities $\cos(x-\frac{\pi}{2}) = \sin x$ and $\sin(x-\frac{\pi}{2}) = -\cos x$ gives the final result:

$\sin(9\theta) - i\cos(9\theta)$

This matches option D.

60913.subject: Mathematics
60913.text: If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, where $f(x) = \dfrac{8^x - 2^x}{k^x - 1}$, for $x \neq 0$ and $f(0) = 2$, then the value of $k$ is...
60913.sol:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, we must have $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = f(0)$.

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8^x - 2^x}{k^x - 1} = 2$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $x$:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{8^x - 1}{x} - \dfrac{2^x - 1}{x}}{\dfrac{k^x - 1}{x}} = 2$

Using the standard limit $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{a^x - 1}{x} = \ln a$:

$\dfrac{\ln 8 - \ln 2}{\ln k} = 2$

$\dfrac{\ln \left(\dfrac{8}{2}\right)}{\ln k} = 2$

$\dfrac{\ln 4}{\ln k} = 2$

$\ln 4 = 2 \ln k$

$\ln 4 = \ln(k^2)$

$k^2 = 4$

Since $k > 0$ for the exponential function $k^x$ to be defined for all real $x$, we get $k = 2$.

61066.subject: Mathematics
61066.sol:
The integral $I = \int_0^2 \frac{3x+1}{x^2+4} dx$ separates into two components:

$I = \int_0^2 \frac{3x}{x^2+4} dx + \int_0^2 \frac{1}{x^2+4} dx$

For the first term, substitute $u = x^2 + 4$ so that $du = 2x dx$ and $x dx = \frac{1}{2} du$:
When $x = 0$, $u = 4$
When $x = 2$, $u = 8$
This yields $\frac{3}{2} \int_4^8 \frac{1}{u} du = \frac{3}{2} \ln\left|u\right| \Big|_4^8 = \frac{3}{2} (\ln 8 - \ln 4) = \frac{3}{2} \ln 2 = \ln(2\sqrt{2})$

The second term follows the standard form:
$\int_0^2 \frac{1}{x^2+4} dx = \frac{1}{2} \arctan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right) \Big|_0^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} - 0\right) = \frac{\pi}{8}$

The complete integral evaluates to $\ln(2\sqrt{2}) + \frac{\pi}{8}$, matching option C.

61347.subject: Mathematics
61347.text: A particular solution of $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}=(x+9 \mathrm{y})^2$, when $x=0, \mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{27}$ is
61347.sol:
Consider the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d}x} = (x + 9y)^2$. Use the substitution $v = x + 9y$ to transform it into a separable equation.

Differentiating $v$ with respect to $x$ gives $\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 + 9\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d}x}$, from which $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d}x} = \frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} - 1\right)$.

Substituting into the original equation yields $\frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} - 1\right) = v^2$, rearranged as $\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = 9v^2 + 1$.

This is separable: $\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{9v^2 + 1} = \mathrm{d}x$. Integrate both sides:

$\int \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{9v^2 + 1} = \int \mathrm{d}x$.
The left integral uses the standard form $\int \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{a^2 + u^2} = \frac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\frac{u}{a}\right)$ with $u = 3v$, $a = 1$, and $\mathrm{d}v = \frac{1}{3} \mathrm{d}u$, resulting in $\frac{1}{3}\arctan(3v) = x + C$, where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Multiply by 3 and solve for $v$: $\arctan(3v) = 3x + K$, so $3v = \tan(3x + K)$.

Substitute back $v = x + 9y$: $3(x + 9y) = \tan(3x + K)$, or equivalently, $3x + 27y = \tan(3x + K)$.

With initial condition $x = 0$, $y = \frac{1}{27}$, substitute and solve: $1 = \tan(K)$, giving $K = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

The particular solution is $3x + 27y = \tan\left(3x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
Comparing with the options, only A: $3x + 27y = \tan\left[3\left(x + \frac{\pi}{12}\right)\right] = \tan\left(3x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ matches.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

62150.sol:
Using the property $e^{\log f(x)} = f(x)$, the given integral simplifies to:

$\int x(\sin x + \cos x) dx$

Applying integration by parts, taking $x$ as the first function and $(\sin x + \cos x)$ as the second function:

$\int x(\sin x + \cos x) dx = x \int (\sin x + \cos x) dx - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dx}(x) \int (\sin x + \cos x) dx \right) dx$

$= x(\sin x - \cos x) - \int 1 \cdot (\sin x - \cos x) dx$

$= x(\sin x - \cos x) - (-\cos x - \sin x) + c$

$= x(\sin x - \cos x) + (\sin x + \cos x) + c$

Answer: $x(\sin x - \cos x) + (\sin x + \cos x) + c$

63603.subject: Mathematics
63603.text: Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from fair playing 52 cards. let X denote number of kings obtained when two cards are drawn, then $\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{X}^2\right)=$
63603.sol:
Let $X$ represent the number of kings obtained when drawing two cards with replacement from a standard 52-card deck. The probability of drawing a king is $P(K) = \frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}$, while the probability of not drawing a king is $P(K') = \frac{12}{13}$.

Since the draws are independent, the probability distribution of $X$ is given by:

$P(X=0) = P(K') \times P(K') = \frac{12}{13} \cdot \frac{12}{13} = \frac{144}{169}$

$P(X=1) = P(K)P(K') + P(K')P(K) = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{13} \cdot \frac{12}{13} = \frac{24}{169}$

$P(X=2) = P(K) \times P(K) = \frac{1}{13} \cdot \frac{1}{13} = \frac{1}{169}$

These probabilities sum to $\frac{144+24+1}{169} = 1$, confirming a valid distribution.

The expected value of $X^2$ is calculated as:

$E(X^2) = \sum x^2 P(X=x) = 0^2 \cdot \frac{144}{169} + 1^2 \cdot \frac{24}{169} + 2^2 \cdot \frac{1}{169}$

$E(X^2) = 0 + \frac{24}{169} + \frac{4}{169} = \frac{28}{169}$

The expected value of $X^2$ is $\frac{28}{169}$, corresponding to choice D.

63968.text: In a triangle $A B C$, with usual notation, $\angle B=\pi / 3, \angle C=\pi / 4 . D$ divides $B C$ internally in the ratio 1:3 then $\frac{\sin \angle \mathrm{BAD}}{\sin \angle \mathrm{CAD}}$
63968.sol:
Let $ BAD = \alpha$ and $ CAD = \beta$. Given $ B = \frac{\pi}{3} = 60^{}^{\circ}$ and $ C = \frac{\pi}{4} = 45^{}^{\circ}$ in $\triangle ABC$, with point $D$ dividing $BC$ in ratio $BD:DC = 1:3$.

Applying the Sine Rule
In $\triangle ABD$: $\frac{BD}{\sin \alpha} = \frac{AD}{\sin B}$, so $BD = AD \cdot \frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin B}$.
In $\triangle ACD$: $\frac{DC}{\sin \beta} = \frac{AD}{\sin C}$, so $DC = AD \cdot \frac{\sin \beta}{\sin C}$.

Using the given ratio
Since $\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{1}{3}$:
$\frac{AD \cdot \frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin B}}{AD \cdot \frac{\sin \beta}{\sin C}} = \frac{1}{3}$ → $\frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} \cdot \frac{\sin C}{\sin B} = \frac{1}{3}$

Solving for the required ratio
$\frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{\sin B}{\sin C} = \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{\sin 60^{}^{\circ}}{\sin 45^{}^{\circ}} = \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}}{6}$

64445.text: Let the plane passing through point $(2,1,-1)$ containing line joining the points $(1,3,2)$ and $(1,2,1)$ makes intercepts p,q,r on co-ordinate axes, then $\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{r}=$

Three points on the plane are given: $A = (2,1,-1)$, $B = (1,3,2)$, and $C = (1,2,1)$.
Vectors in the plane are $\mathrm{AB} = (-1,2,3)$ and $\mathrm{AC} = (-1,1,2)$.

The normal vector $\mathrm{n}$ is perpendicular to $\mathrm{AB}$ and $\mathrm{AC}$, found using the cross product:
$\mathrm{n} = \mathrm{AB} \times \mathrm{AC} = \mathbf{i}(2 \cdot 2 - 3 \cdot 1) - \mathbf{j}(-1 \cdot 2 - 3 \cdot (-1)) + \mathbf{k}(-1 \cdot 1 - 2 \cdot (-1)) = (1, -1, 1)$.

Using point $A$ and normal $\mathrm{n} = (1,-1,1)$, the plane equation is $1(x-2) -1(y-1) +1(z+1)=0$.
Simplifying gives $x - y + z = 0$.

The intercepts on the axes are all zero since setting any two variables to zero forces the third to zero.
Therefore, $p + q + r = 0$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{0}$

The equation of the required plane $\begin{aligned} & (x+y+z-1)+\lambda(2 x+3 y+4 z-5)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(1+2 \lambda) x+(1+3 \lambda) y+(1+4 \lambda) z-1-5 \lambda=0 \end{aligned}$

Substituting $\lambda=-\frac{1}{3}$ in (i), we get $\begin{aligned} & \left(1-\frac{2}{3}\right) x+\left(1-\frac{3}{3}\right) y+\left(1-\frac{4}{3}\right) z-1+\frac{5}{3}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x-z+2=0 \end{aligned}$
Its vector equation is $\overline{\mathrm{r}} \cdot(\hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}})+2=0$

65865.text: Using Bohr's atomic model, the orbital period of electron in hydrogen atom in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit is (\epsilon_0$=permittivity of free space, h=Planck's constant, m = mass of electron, e = electronic charge)$
65865.sol:
The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit in Bohr's model is given by $r = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{\pi m e^2}$.

The velocity of the electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit is given by $v = \dfrac{e^2}{2 \epsilon_0 n h}$.

The orbital period $T$ is the time taken to complete one revolution, which is $T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v}$.

Substituting the values of $r$ and $v$:

$T = \dfrac{2\pi \left(\dfrac{\epsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{\pi m e^2}\right)}{\dfrac{e^2}{2 \epsilon_0 n h}}$

$T = \dfrac{2 \epsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{m e^2} \times \dfrac{2 \epsilon_0 n h}{e^2}$

$T = \dfrac{4 \epsilon_0^2 n^3 h^3}{m e^4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4\,\epsilon_0^2 n^3 h^3}{me^4}$

66078.text: Two parallel plate air capacitors of same capacity 'C' are connected in parallel to a battery of e.m.f. ' $E$ '. Then one of the capacitors is completely filled with dielectric material of constant ' $K$ '. The change in the effective capacity of the parallel combination is
66078.sol:
The initial effective capacitance of two identical parallel plate air capacitors in parallel is $C_{\text{initial}} = C + C = 2C$.

After introducing a dielectric with constant $K$ into one capacitor, its capacitance becomes $C_1' = KC$ while the other remains $C_2 = C$. The new effective capacitance is $C_{\text{final}} = KC + C = C(K + 1)$.

The change in effective capacitance is $\Delta C = C_{\text{final}} - C_{\text{initial}} = C(K + 1) - 2C = C(K - 1)$.

This corresponds to option D.

66793.sol:
Analysis of Magnet Falling Through Cut Ring

When a magnet falls through a conducting ring, Faraday's law indicates that a changing magnetic flux induces an electromotive force. For a current to flow, however, the circuit must form a closed loop.

Since the copper ring has a cut, it cannot sustain an induced current. Without current, no opposing magnetic field is generated via Lenz's law.

The magnet experiences only gravitational acceleration, $g$, as no electromagnetic force opposes its motion.

Thus, the correct choice is $\boxed{A}$.

66810.sol:
The mutual inductance $M$ is determined from the induced emf in coil P due to the changing current in coil Q. Given $E_P = 15 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{V}$ and $\frac{dI_Q}{dt} = 10 \, \text{A}/\text{s}$, the relationship $E_P = M \frac{dI_Q}{dt}$ yields $M = \frac{15 \times 10^{-3}}{10} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{H}$.

The magnetic flux $\Phi_Q$ linked with coil Q when a current $I_P = 1.8 \, \text{A}$ flows through coil P is $\Phi_Q = M I_P = (1.5 \times 10^{-3}) \cdot 1.8 = 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \, \text{Wb}$, or $2.7 \, \text{mWb}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{2.7 \, \text{mWb}}$

68518.text: For a particle moving in a circle with constant angular speed, which of the following statements is 'false'?
options: The velocity vector is tangent to the circle.
The acceleration vector is tangent to the circle.
The velocity and acceleration vectors are perpendicular to each other:
The acceleration vector points to the centre of the circle.
68518.sol:
A: The velocity vector is tangent to the circle in all curvilinear motion, including circular motion. This holds for uniform circular motion.

B: The acceleration vector points radially inward as centripetal acceleration, not tangent to the circle. Only a tangential acceleration component would exist if angular speed were changing, which it is not.

C: Since velocity is tangent and acceleration is radial, they are perpendicular at every point.

D: Uniform circular motion produces purely centripetal acceleration directed toward the circle's center.

Statement B is false.

69145.text: Two identical rings A and B of same mass and radius are revolving, ring A arounds its own diameter and ring B about tangential axis in its own plane. Both the rings A and B have same rotational kinetic energy. The ratio of the angular velocity of ring B to that of ring A is
69145.sol:
Moment of inertia of ring A about its diameter is $I_A = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$.

Moment of inertia of ring B about a tangential axis in its own plane is obtained using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_B = I_A + MR^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2$.

Rotational kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.

Given that both rings have the same rotational kinetic energy, $K_A = K_B$:
$\dfrac{1}{2}I_A\omega_A^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}I_B\omega_B^2$

$\dfrac{\omega_B^2}{\omega_A^2} = \dfrac{I_A}{I_B}$

$\dfrac{\omega_B}{\omega_A} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}MR^2}{\dfrac{3}{2}MR^2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

The ratio of the angular velocity of ring B to that of ring A is $1 : \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $1 : \sqrt{3}$

69163.subject: Physics
69163.text: A uniform solid cylinder with radius R and length L has moment of inertia $I_1$ about the axis of the cylinder. A concentric solid cylinder of radius $R/2$ and length $L/2$ is carved out of the original cylinder. If $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of the carved out portion of the cylinder then $I_1/I_2$ is (Both $I_1$ and $I_2$ are about the axis of the cylinder)
69163.sol:
Let the density of the material of the cylinder be $\rho$.

The mass of the original solid cylinder is $M_1 = \rho \pi R^2 L$.
The moment of inertia of the original solid cylinder about its axis is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} M_1 R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} (\rho \pi R^2 L) R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho \pi R^4 L$

The carved out portion is a solid cylinder of radius $R/2$ and length $L/2$. Its mass is:
$M_2 = \rho \pi \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{8} \rho \pi R^2 L$

The moment of inertia of this carved out portion about the same axis is:
$I_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} M_2 \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{8} \rho \pi R^2 L\right) \left(\dfrac{R^2}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{64} \rho \pi R^4 L$

Taking the ratio of $I_1$ to $I_2$:
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \rho \pi R^4 L}{\dfrac{1}{64} \rho \pi R^4 L} = 32$

Thus, the ratio is $32 : 1$.

69726.subject: Physics
69726.text: An ordinary body cools from $4\theta$ to $3\theta$ in 't' minutes. The temperature of the body after next 't' minutes is (Assume Newton's law of cooling and room temperature as $\theta$)
69726.sol:
According to Newton's law of cooling, the temperature $T$ at time $t$ is given by:

$T - T_s = (T_i - T_s)e^{-kt}$

where $T_s$ is the surrounding temperature and $T_i$ is the initial temperature.

For the first $t$ minutes, $T_i = 4\theta$, $T = 3\theta$, and $T_s = \theta$:

$3\theta - \theta = (4\theta - \theta)e^{-kt}$

$2\theta = 3\theta e^{-kt} \Rightarrow e^{-kt} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

For the next $t$ minutes, the initial temperature is $3\theta$. Let the final temperature be $T'$:

$T' - \theta = (3\theta - \theta)e^{-kt}$

$T' - \theta = 2\theta \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{4\theta}{3}$

$T' = \theta + \dfrac{4\theta}{3} = \dfrac{7\theta}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7\theta}{3}$

69743.subject: Physics
69743.text: Two black spheres P & Q have radii in the ratio $4: 3$. The wavelength of maximum intensity of radiation are in the ratio $4: 5$ respectively. The ratio of radiated power by P to Q is
69743.sol:
Wien's Displacement Law relates temperature and peak wavelength as $\lambda_\max T = b$, so $T \propto 1/\lambda_\max$. Given $\lambda_{max,P}/\lambda_{max,Q} = 4/5$, we find $T_P/T_Q = \lambda_{max,Q}/\lambda_{max,P} = 5/4$.

The Stefan-Boltzmann Law gives radiated power $P = \sigma A T^4$. For spheres, $A = 4\pi R^2$, so $P \propto R^2 T^4$. The power ratio is then $P_P/P_Q = (R_P/R_Q)^2 (T_P/T_Q)^4$.

Substituting $R_P/R_Q = 4/3$ and $T_P/T_Q = 5/4$:

$P_P/P_Q = (4/3)^2 (5/4)^4 = (16/9)(625/256)$

69906.subject: Physics
69906.text: The efficiency of Carnot engine which operates between the two temperatures $T_1 = 500$ K and $T_2 = 300$ K is
69906.sol:
The efficiency of a Carnot engine is given by the formula:

$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$

Given the source temperature $T_1 = 500$ K and the sink temperature $T_2 = 300$ K, substituting these values into the formula gives:

$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{300}{500}$

$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{3}{5}$

$\eta = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$

To express the efficiency as a percentage, multiply by $100\%$:

$\eta = 0.4 \times 100\% = 40\%$

Answer: $40\ \%$

69913.subject: Physics
69913.text: An ideal gas with pressure P, volume V and temperature T is expanded isothermally to volume 2V and a final pressure $P_i$. The same gas is expanded adiabatically to a volume 2V then the final pressure is $P_a$. In terms of $\gamma$, the ratio of the two specific heats for the gas, the ratio $P_i / P_a$ is
69913.sol:
For the isothermal expansion, the equation of state is $PV = \text{constant}$.

$P V = P_i (2V)$

$P_i = \dfrac{P}{2}$

For the adiabatic expansion, the equation of state is $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

$P V^{\gamma} = P_a (2V)^{\gamma}$

$P_a = \dfrac{P}{2^{\gamma}}$

Taking the ratio of the two final pressures:

$\dfrac{P_i}{P_a} = \dfrac{\dfrac{P}{2}}{\dfrac{P}{2^{\gamma}}} = 2^{\gamma - 1}$

Answer: $2^{\gamma-1}$

71052.subject: Biology
71052.text: Which one of the following is the most important services provided by an ecosystem?
71052.sol:
Photosynthesis by photoautotrophs is the most important service provided by an ecosystem. It is the fundamental process that captures solar energy and converts it into chemical energy, forming the basis of all food chains and webs. Additionally, it is the primary source of oxygen in the atmosphere, which is essential for the survival of all aerobic organisms. Without photosynthesis, the entire ecosystem would collapse as there would be no primary production to sustain other trophic levels.

Answer: Photosynthesis by photoautotrophs.

71465.subject: Biology
71465.text: Which organic acid is produced at the end of the TCA cycle?
71465.sol:
The TCA (Tricarboxylic Acid) cycle, also known as the Krebs cycle, is a series of chemical reactions used by all aerobic organisms to release stored energy.

The cycle begins with the condensation of acetyl-CoA with oxaloacetic acid to form citric acid.

Through a series of steps involving oxidation and decarboxylation, various intermediates like $\alpha$-ketoglutaric acid, succinic acid, fumaric acid, and malic acid are formed.

In the final step of the cycle, malic acid is oxidized by the enzyme malate dehydrogenase to regenerate oxaloacetic acid.

This regenerated oxaloacetic acid is then ready to combine with another molecule of acetyl-CoA to start the cycle anew. Thus, oxaloacetic acid is the organic acid produced at the end of the TCA cycle.

Answer: Oxaloacetic acid

71955.subject: Chemistry
71955.text: Elements A and B combine to form the ionic compound $\text{A}_x\text{B}_y$. The anions of B are arranged in hcp array and the cations of A occupy all the octahedral voids. Determine the values of x and y.
71955.sol:
Let the number of anions B in the hcp array be $N$.

The number of octahedral voids in a close-packed structure is equal to the number of packing atoms, which is $N$.

Since cations A occupy all the octahedral voids, the number of cations A is also $N$.

The ratio of the number of atoms of A to B is $N : N = 1 : 1$.

Therefore, the formula of the compound is $\text{AB}$, which gives $x = 1$ and $y = 1$.

Answer: $x = 1$ and $y = 1$

72501.subject: Physics
72501.text: Two copper wires of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ (r_1 > r_2$) are subjected to same tension and are plucked. Tansverse waves set up will$
options: travel faster in the thicker wire.
travel faster in the thinner wire.
travel with the same velocity in bothe the wires.
not travel through both the wires.
72501.sol:
The velocity of a transverse wave in a stretched wire is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $T$ is the tension and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

The linear mass density $\mu$ can be expressed as $\mu = \pi r^2 \rho$, where $r$ is the radius of the wire and $\rho$ is the density of the material.

Substituting $\mu$ into the velocity formula gives $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi r^2 \rho}} = \dfrac{1}{r} \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi \rho}}$.

Since both wires are made of copper, their densities $\rho$ are the same. The tension $T$ is also the same for both wires.

Therefore, the velocity $v$ is inversely proportional to the radius $r$, which means $v \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$.

Since the thinner wire has a smaller radius, the transverse wave will travel faster in the thinner wire.

Answer: travel faster in the thinner wire.

73849.subject: General Ability
73849.text: Which one of the following is NOT a basic property of electric charge?
options: Charge on a body is always an integral multiple of an electron or a proton charge
Charges can be created and destroyed in an isolated system
73849.sol:
The basic properties of electric charge are additivity, conservation, and quantization.

Additivity means total charge is the algebraic sum of individual charges.

Conservation of charge states that the total charge of an isolated system remains constant. Charges can neither be created nor destroyed in an isolated system, though equal amounts of positive and negative charges can be created or destroyed together (like in pair production or annihilation).

Quantization means charge is always an integral multiple of the elementary charge (e$).

Therefore, the statement that charges can be created and destroyed in an isolated system is incorrect and is not a property of electric charge.

Answer: Charges can be created and destroyed in an isolated system$

77847.subject: Mathematics
77847.text: What is the maximum number of points of intersection of $5$ circles ?
77847.sol:
Two circles can intersect at a maximum of $2$ distinct points.

To find the maximum number of points of intersection of $5$ circles, we select any $2$ circles from the given $5$ circles and multiply the number of pairs by $2$.

The number of ways to select $2$ circles from $5$ is $^{5}C_{2}$.

Maximum number of points of intersection $= 2 \times ^{5}C_{2}$

$= 2 \times \dfrac{5 \times 4}{2 \times 1}$

$= 20$

Answer: $20$

78924.text: What is the number of solutions of the equation $\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x=1$ for $0 < x < \pi ?$
78924.sol:
We have given, $\cot 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x=1$ (given)
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \cos 2 x \cdot \cot 3 x-\sin 2 x \cdot \sin 3 x=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos (2 x+3 x)=\cos 5 x=0
\end{aligned}$
Hence $5 x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3 \pi}{2}, \frac{5 \pi}{2}, \frac{7 \pi}{2}, \frac{9 \pi}{2}, \ldots$
But $0 < x < \pi\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=\frac{\pi}{10}, \frac{3 \pi}{10}, \frac{5 \pi}{10}, \frac{7 \pi}{10}, \frac{9 \pi}{10}$
Thus only five values of $x$ are possible.

81362.subject: Chemistry
81362.text:
Calculate emf of the half cell given below :
$\text{Pt (s)} | \text{H}_2 \text{(g, 2 atm)} | \text{HCl (aq, 0.02 M)}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} = 0$ V
$\left(\text{Given}: \dfrac{2.303\ RT}{F} = 0.059, \log 2 = 0.3010\right)$
81362.sol:
The given half-cell is represented as an oxidation electrode: $\text{Pt (s)} | \text{H}_2 \text{(g)} | \text{H}^{+} \text{(aq)}$.

The corresponding oxidation half-cell reaction is:
$\text{H}_2 \text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H}^{+} \text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^{-}$

Using the Nernst equation for the oxidation potential:
$E = E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log \dfrac{[\text{H}^{+}]^2}{P_{\text{H}_2}}$

Given values:
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^{+}} = 0$ V
$n = 2$
$[\text{H}^{+}] = 0.02$ M (since HCl is a strong monoprotic acid)
$P_{\text{H}_2} = 2$ atm

Substituting the values into the Nernst equation:
$E = 0 - \dfrac{0.059}{2} \log \dfrac{(0.02)^2}{2}$

$E = -0.0295 \log \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-4}}{2}$

$E = -0.0295 \log (2 \times 10^{-4})$

$E = -0.0295 (\log 2 + \log 10^{-4})$

$E = -0.0295 (0.3010 - 4)$

$E = -0.0295 \times (-3.699)$

$E = 0.10912$ V $\approx 0.109$ V

Answer: $0.109$ V

84375.text: At a particular locus, frequency of $A$ allele is 0.6 and that of a is 0.4 . What would be the frequency of heterozygotes in a random mating population at equilibrium?
84375.sol:
In a stable population, for a gene with two alleles, 'A' (dominant) and 'a' (recessive),
the frequency of ' $\mathrm{A}^{\prime}=\mathrm{p}$
the frequency of ' $a$ ' $=q$,
According Hardy-Weinberg equation:

$\mathrm{p}^$2+2 p q+q²=1

where $\mathrm{p}^2=$ Frequency of $\mathrm{A}$ (homozygous dominant) individuals $\mathrm{q}^2=$ Frequency of aa (homozygous recessive) individuals
$2 \mathrm{pq}=$ Frequency of $\mathrm{Aa}$ (heterozygous) individuals.

$\begin{aligned}$& \therefore 2 $\mathrm{pq}(\text{ frequency$ of heterozygote })=\\
& 2 $\times$0.6 $\times$0.4=0.48
\end{aligned}

Number of moles of ${H}_{2}S{O}_{4}$ before electrolysis

Hence, moles of ${H}_{2}S{O}_{4}$ used $= 0.56$
Remaining mol of ${H}_{2}S{O}_{4} = 7.5 - 0.56 = 6.94$
Final molarity $= \dfrac{n}{V} \times 1000 = \dfrac{6.94}{1.5 \times 1000} \times 1000$
$= 4.626$

92683.text: A ball falls freely from a height of $45m$. When the ball is at a height of $25m$, it explodes into two equal pieces. 92683.sol:
Let at the time explosion velocity of one piece of mass is (10$\overset{^}{i}$). If the velocity of other be ${\overset{→}{v}}_{2}$, then from conservation law of momentum (since there is no force in the horizontal direction), the horizontal component of ${\overset{→}{v}}_{2}$, must be $- 10\overset{^}{i}$.

$∴$ The relative velocity of two parts in the horizontal direction $= 20ms^{- 1}$

Time taken by the ball to fall through 45 m,

$= t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 45}{10}} = 3s$ and time taken by the ball to fall through first 20m, $t^{′} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h′}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 20}{10}} = 2s$. Hence time taken by ball pieces to fall from 25 m height to ground $= t - t^{′} = 3 - 2 = 1s$.

$∴$ The horizontal distance between the two pieces at the time of striking on the ground

$= 20 \times 1 = 20$ m

94962.text:
In a special arrangement of Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between the slits $d$ is twice the distance between the screen and the slits $D$, i.e $d = 2D$. For this setup, the value of $D$ such that the first minima on the screen fall at a distance $D$ from the centre $O$ is found to be $\dfrac{\lambda}{N}$.

What is the value of $N$? [Take $\sqrt{5} = 2 . 24$]
94962.sol:
From diagram as provided in question, $OP = x$
$CO = D$
${S}_{1}C = {S}_{2}C = D{T}_{1}P = {T}_{1}O - OP = D - x$
${T}_{2}P = {T}_{2}O + OP = D + x$
Now, ${S}_{1}p = \sqrt{{\left({S}_{1}{T}_{1}\right)}^{2} + {\left({T}_{1}P\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}}$

${S}_{2}P = \sqrt{{\left({S}_{2}{T}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({T}_{2}P\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}}$

For fist minimum to occur,

Path difference

${S}_{2}P - {S}_{1}P = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

The first minimum falls at a distance $D$ from the centre, i.e., $x = D$

$\left[{D}^{2} + 4{D}^{2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2} - D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$∴ D\left(\sqrt{5} - 1\right) = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\left(2 . 24 - 1\right)} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2 . 48}$

Assertion : On a curved path, average speed of a particle can never be equal to average velocity.
Reason : Average speed is total distance travelled divided by total time. Whereas average velocity is final velocity, plus initial velocity divided by two.

If both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true
100256.sol:
Assertion is true: On a curved path, the displacement (a straight line from start to end) is always less than the distance traveled along the curve. 101297.subject: Physics
101297.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If$E$be the total energy of a satellite moving around the earth, then its potential energy will be $\dfrac{E}{2}$.

Statement II: The kinetic energy of a satellite revolving in an orbit is equal to the half the magnitude of total energy $E$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
101297.sol:
Let $m$ be the mass of the satellite.

The potential energy of the satellite is 

$U = \dfrac{- GMm}{r}$

The velocity of the satellite is given by 

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$

Kinetic energy is given by

$K = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{m}{2}\dfrac{GM}{r} = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$

The total mechanical energy is the sum of potential and kinetic energy. So,

$T = K + U = \dfrac{GMm}{2r} - \dfrac{GMm}{r} = - \dfrac{GMm}{2r}$

Hence, both the statements are false.

101403.subject: Physics
101403.text: A planet of mass $81M$ and its moon of mass $M$ are separated by a distance $10d$. A spaceship of mass $m$ is parked on the line joining them at a point where the net gravitational force on it is zero. What is the gravitational potential energy of the spaceship at this position?
101403.sol:
Let the spaceship be at a distance $x$ from the planet. The net gravitational force on it is zero, so the gravitational fields of the planet and the moon must be equal in magnitude at this point.

$\dfrac{G(81M)m}{x^2} = \dfrac{GMm}{(10d - x)^2}$

Taking the square root of both sides:
$\dfrac{9}{x} = \dfrac{1}{10d - x}$

$\Rightarrow 90d - 9x = x$
$\Rightarrow 10x = 90d \Rightarrow x = 9d$

The spaceship is at a distance of $9d$ from the planet and $10d - 9d = d$ from the moon.

The gravitational potential energy $U$ of the spaceship is the scalar sum of the potential energies due to both bodies:
$U = -\dfrac{G(81M)m}{9d} - \dfrac{GMm}{d}$

$U = -\dfrac{9GMm}{d} - \dfrac{GMm}{d} = -\dfrac{10GMm}{d}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{10GMm}{d}$

102021.subject: Physics
102021.text: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is taken through a cycle $A B C D A$ as shown in the $p$-V diagram. Column II gives the characteristics involved in the cycle. Match them with each of the processes given in Column I.
102021.sol:
Internal energy $\propto T \propto p V$
This is because
$U=\frac{n f}{2} R T=\frac{f}{2} p V$
Here, $n=$ number of moles
$f=$ degree of freedom
If the product $p V$ increases, then internal energy will increase and if product decreases, the internal energy will decrease.
Further, work is done on the gas, if volume of gas decreases. For heat exchange.
$Q=W+\Delta U$
Work done is area under $p-V$ graph. If volume increases work done by gas is positive and if volume decreases work done by gas is negative. Further $\Delta U$ is positive if product of $p V$ is increasing and $N U$ is negative, if product of $p V$ is decreasing. If heat is taken by the gas $Q$ is positive and if heat is lost by the gas $Q$ is negative.
Keeping the above points in mind the answer to this question is as under.
(A) $\rightarrow(\mathrm{p}, \mathrm{r}, \mathrm{t})$
(B) $\rightarrow(\mathrm{p}, \mathrm{r})$
(C) $\rightarrow$ (q, s)
(D) $\rightarrow(\mathrm{r}, \mathrm{t})$
Analysis of Question
(i) Calculation wise, question is slightly lengthy. Otherwise question is theory based and simple.
(ii) In process $D A$,
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & & p_A V_A & =p_D V_D \\ \therefore & & T_A & =T_D \\ \text{ or } & \Delta U & =0\end{array}$
Further, volume of gas is decreasing. Therefore, work is done on the gas or work done by gas is negative. Therefore, $Q is negative or heat is lost.
(iii) This question covers almost all the concepts of first law of thermodynamics.$

102424.subject: Physics
102424.text: The variation of the square of the time period ($T^2$) with the length ($l$) of a simple pendulum is plotted for two different planets, A and B. The resulting graphs are straight lines passing through the origin, making angles of $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ respectively with the $l$-axis. If a block is dropped from the same height $h$ on both planets, what is the ratio of the time of fall on planet A to that on planet B?
102424.sol:
For a simple pendulum, the time period $T$ is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $T^2 = \left(\dfrac{4\pi^2}{g}\right)l$.

The graph of $T^2$ versus $l$ is a straight line with slope $m = \tan\theta = \dfrac{4\pi^2}{g}$.

Thus, the acceleration due to gravity $g \propto \dfrac{1}{\tan\theta}$.

For planet A: $g_A \propto \dfrac{1}{\tan 30^\circ} = \sqrt{3}$.

For planet B: $g_B \propto \dfrac{1}{\tan 60^\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The ratio of accelerations due to gravity is $\dfrac{g_A}{g_B} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1/\sqrt{3}} = 3$.

The time of fall from a height $h$ is $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$, which means $t \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{g}}$.

Therefore, the ratio of the times of fall is $\dfrac{t_A}{t_B} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g_B}{g_A}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The ratio is $1 : \sqrt{3}$.

Answer: $1 : \sqrt{3}$

103574.subject: Physics
103574.text: The turns of a solenoid, designed to provide a given magnetic flux density along its axis, are wound to fill the space between two concentric cylinders of fixed radii. How should the diameter $d$ of the wire used be chosen so as to minimize the heat dissipated in the windings?
options: Wire should be multiple of $5 d$
103574.sol: The cross-sectional area of the space to be filled is fixed, whilst that of the wire varies as $d^2$. Thus, $n \propto d^{-2}$. The resistance of one turn is inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area of the wire, i.e. varies as $d^{-2}$ and hence the resistance per unit length of the solenoid is $R \propto n d^{-2} \propto d^{-4}$. The flux density $B$ is $\propto n I$ and therefore the required current $I \propto n^{-1} \propto d^2$. The heat dissipated per unit length is $R I^2$, which $\propto d^{-4}\left(d^2\right)^2$, i.e. independent of $d$. Thus, within limits, it does not matter what diameter wire is chosen so far as the heating effect is concerned.

103849.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The mutual inductance of coil 1 with respect to coil 2 is the same as mutual inductance of coil 2 with respect to coil 1.
Reason (R) : Mutual inductance between coils is independent of current passing through the coil In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
103849.sol:
- Assertion (A) states that the mutual inductance of coil 1 with respect to coil 2 is the same as the mutual inductance of coil 2 with respect to coil 1 ($M_{12} = M_{21}$). This is a fundamental property of mutual inductance, often referred to as the reciprocity theorem for mutual inductance. So, Assertion (A) is true.
- Reason (R) states that mutual inductance between coils is independent of the current passing through the coil. Mutual inductance (M) is a geometric and physical property of the coil arrangement (number of turns, area, separation, core material, etc.). It describes how effectively the magnetic flux produced by one coil links with another. It does not depend on the actual current flowing in the coils. So, Reason (R) is true.
However, Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

104136.subject: Physics
104136.text: A coil is connected to a $12\text{ V}$ DC source and draws a steady current of $4\text{ A}$. When the same coil is connected to an AC source of $12\text{ V}$ (rms) and angular frequency $50\text{ rad/s}$, the rms current in the circuit is $2.4\text{ A}$. The inductance of the coil is:
104136.sol:
When the coil is connected to a DC source, the inductive reactance is zero. The resistance $R$ of the coil is:
$R = \dfrac{V_{DC}}{I_{DC}} = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3\ \Omega$

When connected to an AC source, the net impedance $Z$ of the coil is:
$Z = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{I_{rms}} = \dfrac{12}{2.4} = 5\ \Omega$

The impedance of the coil (which acts as a series LR circuit) is given by:
$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$
$5 = \sqrt{3^2 + X_L^2}$
$25 = 9 + X_L^2 \Rightarrow X_L^2 = 16 \Rightarrow X_L = 4\ \Omega$

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L$. Substituting the given values:
$4 = 50 \times L$
$L = \dfrac{4}{50}\text{ H} = 0.08\text{ H} = 80\text{ mH}$

Answer: $80\text{ mH}$

104952.sol:
$( A )$ True, an atom of each element emits a characteristic spectrum.

$( B )$ True, according to Bohr's postulates $mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ and hence electron resides into orbits of specific radius called stationary orbits.

105603.subject: Physics
105603.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V$ and strikes a target to produce continuous X-rays. If $\lambda_{d}$ is the de Broglie wavelength of the incident electron and $\lambda_{min}$ is the minimum wavelength of the emitted X-rays, then the ratio $\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\lambda_{min}}$ is proportional to:
105603.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference $V$ is given by:
$\lambda_{d} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}$

The minimum wavelength of the continuous X-rays produced is given by equating the maximum photon energy to the electron's kinetic energy:
$\lambda_{min} = \dfrac{hc}{eV}$

Taking the ratio of the two wavelengths:
$\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\lambda_{min}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}}{\dfrac{hc}{eV}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\lambda_{min}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}} \times \dfrac{eV}{hc} = \dfrac{1}{c}\sqrt{\dfrac{eV}{2m}}$

Since $h$, $c$, $e$, and $m$ are constants, the ratio $\dfrac{\lambda_{d}}{\lambda_{min}}$ is directly proportional to $\sqrt{V}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{V}$

108715.subject: Chemistry
108715.text: Which thermodynamic parameter is not a state function?
108715.sol:
$H$ and $U$ are state functions but $W$ and $q$ are not state functions.
From the equation, $\Delta H=\Delta U+\Delta P V$ 
At constant pressure, $\Delta H=\Delta U+P \Delta V$ 
At constant volume, $\Delta H=\Delta U+V \Delta P$ 
At constant pressure, $\Delta P=0, \Delta H=q_p$
so, it is a state function.
At constant volume, $\Delta V=0, \Delta U=q_v$ so, it is a state function.
Work done in any adiabatic process is state function.
$\Delta U=q-W \quad(\because q=0)$
$\Delta U=-W$
Work done in isothermal process is not a state function.
$W=-q \quad(\because \Delta T=0, q \neq 0)$

108949.subject: Chemistry
108949.text:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A) : Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Reason (R) : Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
108949.sol:
- Assertion (A): Solubility of a gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
Correct.
Most gases dissolve in water exothermically. According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the opposite direction (less dissolution), hence solubility decreases.
- Reason (R): Dissolution of a gas in water is an exothermic process.
Correct.
Heat is released when gas molecules are captured by water molecules (due to intermolecular attractions).
Here, (R) correctly explains (A) \(\rightarrow\) higher temperature adds heat, so equilibrium shifts to gas phase, reducing solubility.

$\mathrm{Na} + \mathrm{C} + \mathrm{N} + \mathrm{S} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaSCN}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + \mathrm{SCN}^{-} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}$

If excess sodium were used, the thiocyanate would decompose into cyanide and sulphide, yielding the standard independent tests.

Answer: $\mathrm{NaSCN}$, Blood red

121590.subject: Botany
121590.text: In R.H. Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification, fungi were removed from the plant kingdom and placed in a distinct kingdom of their own. Which of the following pairs of main criteria primarily justified this separation?
options: Cell structure and Mode of nutrition
Mode of nutrition and Phylogenetic relationships
121590.sol:
Earlier classification systems placed fungi and green plants together despite fundamental differences. When Whittaker's criteria were applied, fungi were separated into Kingdom Fungi primarily due to two major differences:
1. Mode of nutrition: Fungi are heterotrophic, whereas green plants are autotrophic.
2. Cell structure: Fungi possess a chitinous cell wall, whereas green plants have a cellulosic cell wall.

Body organisation is not the primary distinguishing factor here, as both groups largely consist of multicellular or tissue-level organisms. Thus, cell structure and mode of nutrition were the primary criteria justifying their separation.

Answer: Cell structure and Mode of nutrition

123860.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells in the quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G}_0$) are considered to be in an inactive stage of the cell cycle.
Reason (R): Cells in the $\mathrm{G}_0$ phase are metabolically inactive and permanently lose their capacity to proliferate.

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
123860.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct because cells that do not divide further exit the $\mathrm{G}_1$ phase and enter an inactive stage of the cell cycle known as the quiescent stage ($\mathrm{G}_0$).

Reason (R) is incorrect because cells in the $\mathrm{G}_0$ stage remain metabolically active. Furthermore, they do not permanently lose their capacity to proliferate; they can resume division if called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

123901.subject: Botany
123901.text: An onion root tip cell has $16$ chromosomes and its DNA content is $2\text{C}$ at the $\text{G}_{1}$ phase of the cell cycle. What will be the number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA in this cell at the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase?
123901.sol:
During the S phase of the cell cycle, DNA replication occurs, causing the amount of DNA per cell to double. Therefore, the DNA content increases from $2\text{C}$ to $4\text{C}$.

However, the number of chromosomes does not increase because the newly synthesized sister chromatids remain attached at the same centromere. Thus, the chromosome number remains $16$.

Since the $\text{G}_{2}$ phase directly follows the S phase, the cell will have $16$ chromosomes and $4\text{C}$ DNA.

Answer: $16$ chromosomes and $4\text{C}$ DNA

124923.subject: Botany
124923.text: When are large volumes of gases exchanged in plants?
124923.sol: Yes, plants require O2 for respiration to occur and they also give out CO2. Hence, plants have systems in place that ensure the availability of O2. Plants, unlike animals, have no specialized organs for gaseous exchange but they have stomata and lenticels for this purpose. There are several reasons why plants can get along without respiratory organs. First, each plant part takes care of its own gas-exchange needs. There is very little transport of gases from one plant part to another. Second, plants do not present great demands for gas exchange. Roots, stems and leaves respire at rates far lower than animals do. Only during photosynthesis are large volumes of gases exchanged and, each leaf is well adapted to take care of its own needs during these periods. When cells photosynthesize, availability of O2 is not a problem in these cells since O2 is released within the cell

125963.subject: Botany
125963.text: What is the final product of sexual reproduction in angiosperms?
125963.sol: In angiosperms, the seed is the final product of sexual reproduction. It is often described as a fertilised ovule. Seeds are formed inside fruits. A seed typically consists of seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis. The cotyledons (Figure 1.15a) of the embryo are simple structures, generally thick and swollen due to storage of food reserves (as in legumes). Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Nonalbuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor). Occasionally, in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also persistent.

127784.text:
A sparrow can function as a primary consumer when it feeds on seeds, and as a secondary consumer when it feeds on herbivorous insects. Consider a crop field where the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is $20,000\text{ J}$.

What will be the energy available to the sparrow when it feeds exclusively on the seeds (Case I) and when it feeds exclusively on the herbivorous insects (Case II), respectively?
127784.sol:
In Case I, the sparrow feeds on seeds, acting as a primary consumer (second trophic level, $T_2$).
Energy available at $T_1$ (NPP of crop) = $20,000\text{ J}$.
According to the 10 percent law, energy available to the sparrow = $10\%$ of $20,000\text{ J} = 2,000\text{ J}$.

In Case II, the sparrow feeds on herbivorous insects, acting as a secondary consumer (third trophic level, $T_3$).
Energy available to insects ($T_2$) = $10\%$ of $20,000\text{ J} = 2,000\text{ J}$.
Energy available to the sparrow ($T_3$) = $10\%$ of $2,000\text{ J} = 200\text{ J}$.

Therefore, the energy available in Case I and Case II is $2,000\text{ J}$ and $200\text{ J}$, respectively.

Answer: $2,000\text{ J}$ and $200\text{ J}$

127789.subject: Botany
127789.text:
Read the following statements carefully:
A. The unit of productivity can be expressed as $\text{g m}^{-2} \text{yr}^{-1}$.
B. Gross primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.
C. Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
D. Net primary productivity minus respiration losses equals Gross primary productivity.

How many of the above statements are correct?
127789.sol:
Statement A is correct. Productivity is the rate of biomass production, and it is expressed in terms of $\text{g m}^{-2} \text{yr}^{-1}$ or $(\text{kcal m}^{-2}) \text{yr}^{-1}$.

Statement B is incorrect. Net primary productivity (NPP), not gross primary productivity (GPP), is the available biomass for consumption by heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).

Statement C is correct. Secondary productivity is defined exactly as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Statement D is incorrect. The correct relationship is GPP minus respiration losses (R) equals NPP (GPP - R = NPP). Therefore, GPP equals NPP + R, not NPP - R.

Exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Only two

127793.subject: Botany
127793.text: In a typical aquatic food chain, which of the following organisms occupies the second trophic level?
127793.sol:
In an aquatic ecosystem, the grazing food chain typically follows this sequence:

Phytoplankton $\rightarrow$ Zooplankton $\rightarrow$ Small fishes $\rightarrow$ Large fishes

The first trophic level ($T_1$) is occupied by producers, which are the phytoplankton. The second trophic level ($T_2$) is occupied by primary consumers, which are the zooplankton. Small fishes act as secondary consumers and occupy the third trophic level ($T_3$), while large fishes act as tertiary consumers at the fourth trophic level ($T_4$).

Students often confuse the second trophic level with secondary consumers (small fishes), but the second trophic level always corresponds to primary consumers.

Answer: Zooplankton

Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body. 128932.subject: Zoology
128932.text: What decreases the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction of action potential?
128932.sol: Normal activities of the heart are regulated intrinsically, i.e., auto regulated by specialised muscles (nodal tissue), hence the heart is called myogenic. A special neural centre in the medulla oblangata can moderate the cardiac function through autonomic nervous system (ANS). Neural signals through the sympathetic nerves (part of ANS) can increase the rate of heart beat, the strength of ventricular contraction and thereby the cardiac output. On the other hand, parasympathetic neural signals (another component of ANS) decrease the rate of heart beat, speed of conduction of action potential and thereby the cardiac output. Adrenal medullary hormones can also increase the cardiac output.

129561.subject: Zoology
129561.text: What is the role of the CNS in the release of urine from the bladder?
options: It initiates the contraction of smooth muscles of the bladder
It stimulates the urethral sphincter to relax
129561.sol: Urine formed by the nephrons is ultimately carried to the urinary bladder where it is stored till a voluntary signal is given by the central nervous system (CNS). This signal is initiated by the stretching of the urinary bladder as it gets filled with urine. In response, the stretch receptors on the walls of the bladder send signals to the CNS. The CNS passes on motor messages to initiate the contraction of smooth muscles of the bladder and simultaneous relaxation of the urethral sphincter causing the release of urine. The process of release of urine is called micturition and the neural mechanisms causing it is called the micturition reflex. An adult human excretes, on an average, 1 to 1.5 litres of urine per day. The urine formed is a light yellow coloured watery fluid which is slightly acidic (pH-6.0) and has a characterestic odour. On an average, 25-30 gm of urea is excreted out per day. Various conditions can affect the characteristics of urine. Analysis of urine helps in clinical diagnosis of many metabolic discorders as well as malfunctioning of the kidney. For example, presence of glucose (Glycosuria) and ketone bodies (Ketonuria) in urine are indicative of diabetes mellitus.
